name: MOONSHOT

_THESIS.in_one_line: A memecoin resolves in the first half hour. Either it runs or it is dead money. Stop holding it for eight.
_THESIS.what_is_new: Nothing in this lab tests speed. A2 holds 12h, E2 and F2 hold 8h, C2 and D2 hold 4h, B2 holds 2h. All six sit through the dead time. G1 is the first book built around fast resolution, an uncapped runner, and a floor that ratchets up.
_THESIS.what_it_replaces: F2 capped every winner at +30%. Four of its 22 take-profit exits went on to +72%, +118%, +206% and +214% after it sold. The cap gave away the entire tail, and the tail is where the money is.

entry_gate._why_unchanged: F2's gate is the one component with evidence behind it. It rejects 98% of candidates on liquidity and it is why F2 is the only book that did not collapse. Keep it.

sizing._why_scale: A ratcheting book that never raises its bet never compounds. Position is 1% of CURRENT equity, so as the book climbs the bet climbs with it.

exits._ordering: Checked every observation, in this order. First match wins.

abandon_if_flat._why: The moon-or-nothing rule. Median time to +30% is 19.7 minutes; a token that has not moved 8% in ten is not the one. Exit, free the capital, take the next candidate.

scale_out._why: Selling 75% at +30% returns 97.5% of the stake. From that moment the remaining 25% is a free ride and cannot lose real money.

runner._why: No cap on the remaining 25%. A 45% trail is wide enough to sit through the volatility that a 20% trail exits on. This is the only part of the book that can produce a large day.

exits._why_45: Time to +30%: median 19.7 min, p75 29.3, p90 60. A 45-minute box holds ~90% of every winner that was ever going to win and none of the dead time.

_why_no_cap: At 45-minute holds the book turns over fast by design. Capping entries would throttle the only engine it has.

equity_ratchet._why: This is the 'goes up, does not go down' mechanism. The floor tracks the book's high-water mark minus 3% and NEVER moves down. Book hits $1,100, floor becomes $1,067. Book hits $1,400, floor becomes $1,358. A run can be given back 3% and no more.
equity_ratchet._why_no_force_close: Force-closing sells every open position at once into pools that may already be dead. That is the exact mechanism that produced the -100% rows. The floor stops new risk; it never panic-sells.

_HOW_TO_JUDGE_IT_IN_THREE_DAYS.trade_count: 45-minute holds at F2's entry rate should produce 250-400 closed trades in 3 days. That is a real sample, not 60.
_HOW_TO_JUDGE_IT_IN_THREE_DAYS.the_number_that_matters: mean net per trade. Not equity, which one runner can distort.
_HOW_TO_JUDGE_IT_IN_THREE_DAYS.what_good_looks_like: positive mean per trade across 250+ trades, with the runner tail present rather than one lucky token carrying it.
_HOW_TO_JUDGE_IT_IN_THREE_DAYS.what_failure_looks_like: the abandon rule fires on 80%+ of entries and each one costs friction. If that happens the 10-minute/8% threshold is wrong, and that is a single number to move.
_HOW_TO_JUDGE_IT_IN_THREE_DAYS.honest_caveat: This is the first design in this lab built on speed and an uncapped tail, and both are supported by your own measurements. It is not a guarantee. It will be measurable in three days, which the 8-hour books never were.

_DEPENDENCY.blocking: The dead-pool valuation bug must be fixed first. F2's reported friction is 9.3% of notional against a model that says 0.84%. G1 holds for 45 minutes instead of 8 hours, so it is far less exposed to the max_hold path where that bug lives — but if it ships onto the broken valuation its runner leg will book fake proceeds the same way C2 and D2 did.
_DEPENDENCY.minimum: If the fix is not ready, ship G1 anyway but read ONLY its mean-per-trade with the runner leg excluded, until the valuation is trustworthy.

learning._what_it_does: G1 watches what happens to the tokens it trades and moves its own parameters when the evidence says they are wrong. Two loops are live.

abandon_calibration._how: Compares how often ABANDONED tokens later ran (+30%) against how often HELD tokens died. If it is cutting winners it loosens; if it is holding losers it tightens. This is the only G1 constant that was a guess rather than a measurement, which is why it is the one that learns.

regime_monitor._how: Tracks whether the feed is producing runners at all. When the rate of tokens reaching +30% falls significantly below baseline, position size halves - the tail G1 depends on is not there this week. It never scales UP on a hot streak.

safety.requires_significance: two-proportion z >= 1.96, not a point estimate
safety.audit_trail: every change records old value, new value, sample size, z-score and the reason
safety._why: This project has twice been burned by fitting to a small sample - a $300k liquidity floor on n=28 from a single day, and a positive F2 read on 14 trades. An unbounded learner would automate that mistake. It adapts over days, not minutes.

_what_is_NOT_learned_yet.which_token_to_buy: Not built, and the reason is a measurement. Over 559 v2 trades, permutation tests (20k iterations) on every recorded entry-time variable: liquidity p=0.3914, entry slippage p=0.4517, detect-to-open delay p=0.4500, stake p=0.1133. Nothing separates total losses from survivors, so a classifier over these features would learn noise and report confidence while doing it.
_what_is_NOT_learned_yet.what_would_unlock_it: top-10 holder concentration and LP lock status at entry. Neither is recorded anywhere today. Record them for ~200 trades and entry classification becomes buildable on evidence instead of hope.
